newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks tumble at opening on interest rate fear.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks tumble at opening on interest rate fear.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks tumbled at the opening on Monday on renewed fear of an interest rate rise, with the blue chip Hang Seng Index falling 309 points, or 1.86 percent, to 16,338 in early trade.
"The main reason for the fall is the sharp decline on Wall Street and the sharp increase in the U.S. long bond yield on Friday night," said Percy Au-Young Ping, research director at DBS Securities.
The Dow industrials fell 156.78 points, or 1.91 percent, to 8,031.22 on Friday under the mounting pressure of interest rate rises following the latest spate of strong U.S. economic data.
Yields on the U.S. 30-year bond rose to a high of 6.66 percent before closing at 6.64 percent on Friday.
Interest rate-sensitive property counters were hit hardest, with Cheung Kong losing HK$2.50 to HK$93.75.
Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$3.00 to HK$101.50.
HSBC's increase of its mortgage rate last Friday by 25 basis points also affected sentiment, Au-Young said.

"HSBC's decision indicates the banking industry is under some pressure to control mortgage lending carefully and also indicates the SAR government is very serious about cooling down property prices further," he said.
HSBC dropped HK$4.00 to HK$269.00 and its unit Hang Seng Bank eased HK$0.50 to HK$102.50.
"Bargain hunting emerged at dips and lifted the Hang Seng Index from its lows," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities.
But the selling may not be finished because additional U.S. economic data, which could affect the interest rate trend, would be released this week, he said.
China related stocks were lower on profit-taking.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index for H-shares eased 12 points, or 0.96 percent, to 1,330 and the red-chip Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporation Index eased 21 points, to 3,686.87.
